units.text: The amendment on congressional pay was originally proposed in 1789 as one of twelve Madison-era proposals; ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, leaving the pay amendment unratified until 1992.

citations.title: Constitutional Amendments – Amendment 27 – “Financial Compensation for the Congress” | Ronald Reagan
Interpretation: The Twenty-Seventh Amendment | Constitution Center

judgement.reason: The passages state that Madison proposed twelve amendments in 1789, ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights excluding the congressional pay amendment, and that the pay amendment finally gained ratification by three-fourths of states in 1992.

units.text: The amendment became part of the Constitution in 1992 after 3/4 of states ratified it, confirmed by the Archivist's certification and multiple sources stating the 1992 ratification date.

citations.title: Constitutional Amendments – Amendment 27 – “Financial Compensation for the Congress” | Ronald Reagan

judgement.reason: The passages support ratification in 1992 after three-fourths of states and that the amendment became part of the Constitution, but they only state the Archivist was required to issue a certificate, not that he actually did so.
